pages.title: Amantin & Kasei Comm. Bank Limited
pages.content: Our History The bank was first registered as the centre for wealth creation and started operations at Kasei in the Ashanti Region, by then board chairman. There was one commercial bank at Amantin, which later collapsed. The directors of the then centre for wealth creation decided to relocate the financial house to Amantin and the name was then changed to Amantin an Kasei to serve both communities. Amantin is in the Bono East Region and Kasei in the Ashanti Region. It has since it's founding been headquartered at the Amantin in the Bono East Region. Subscribe to our newsletter Subscribe

pages.title: Amantin & Kasei Comm. Bank Limited
pages.content: Susu Account Susu Account: This is opened for those who want to save or make deposit daily or every weekly. The bank assigns mobile bankers to this type of account holders to collect their deposits as scheduled with them. It helps avoid the burden of walking to the banking hall daily or weekly to make deposits. The Bank recommends maintaining a minimum amount of GHS10 to keep it functioning. The account does not attract interest and withdrawals can be made all times. The account can be used to apply for credit facility. FEATURES AND BENEFITS Minimum opening balance of GHS 10 Unlimited withdrawals SMS alert It does not attract interest The account can be used to apply for credit facility. pages.content: Our News Letter Amantin and Kasei community bank records impressive growth in 2023 ...posts 75% profit growth 2024-09-27, by:web Administrator The Amantin and Kasei Community Bank headquartered at Amantin in the Bono East Region, made impressive strides in key performance metrics during the 2023-year review. The bank reported a remarkable increase in its total advances to businesses and individuals, soaring by an impressive 46.85%. The figure shows a shift from a little over GH 17.25 million in 2022 to approximately GHe25.34million in 2023. Additionally, total deposits also saw a growth, rising from GHe69.40 million to GH 81.52 million-an appreciable change of 17.47%. The Board Chairman of the Bank, Richard Owusu Afriyie, who announced these developments during the 19th annual general meeting of shareholders, held at Amantin said, "the bank performed extremely well.
